diagnostics.title: CORS reflects any origin with credentials enabled
diagnostics.recommendation: Do not combine `credentials: true` with a reflected origin. Use an explicit allowlist (`origin: ['https://app.example.com']`) or a validating function that only calls back `true` for known origins.

diagnostics.title: Async route handler with no error path
diagnostics.recommendation: Wrap the handler (`asyncHandler(fn)` / express-async-errors), or add a `try/catch` that calls `next(error)`, or upgrade to Express 5. A rejection after the first `await` otherwise escapes Express 4 error handling and the request hangs.

diagnostics.title: Response sent in a guard without a return
diagnostics.recommendation: Prefix the guard's response with `return` (`return res.status(400).json(...)`). A response call does not stop the handler — without `return`, the 'rejected' request runs the protected logic and responds twice.

diagnostics.title: Fastify route without a validation schema
diagnostics.recommendation: Attach a JSON `schema` to the route (`{ schema: { body, querystring, params } }`). Fastify validates and serializes against it before the handler runs; without one the route accepts arbitrary input.

diagnostics.title: Nest body param without validation
diagnostics.recommendation: Apply a global `ValidationPipe` (`app.useGlobalPipes(new ValidationPipe())`) and type the parameter with a DTO class (`@Body() dto: CreateUserDto`) so class-validator diagnostics run before the handler.

diagnostics.title: Async callback passed to a synchronous array method
diagnostics.recommendation: Use `for...of` with `await` for sequential work, or `await Promise.all(collection.map(fn))` for parallel work. For an async predicate, resolve first (`const flags = await Promise.all(items.map(pred))`) then filter synchronously.

diagnostics.title: Async function passed as a Promise executor
diagnostics.recommendation: Keep the executor synchronous and do the async work inside with explicit `resolve`/`reject` (`new Promise((resolve, reject) => { work().then(resolve, reject); })`), or drop the constructor and use an async IIFE wrapped in try/catch.

diagnostics.title: Sequential await over independent work in a loop
diagnostics.recommendation: Collect the promises and `await Promise.all(items.map((x) => work(x)))` instead of awaiting inside the loop. If the collection is caller-sized, bound the fan-out with `p-limit`.

diagnostics.title: console.log left in committed code
diagnostics.recommendation: Remove the stray `console.log`/`console.debug`, or route it through a structured logger (`logger.info(...)`). Keep `console.error`/`console.warn` for real findings.

diagnostics.title: Database client/pool constructed inside a handler
diagnostics.recommendation: Construct the client/pool once at module scope and reuse the singleton across requests (e.g. `const prisma = new PrismaClient();`). A per-request client opens a new connection every time and exhausts the pool.

diagnostics.title: async function with no await
diagnostics.recommendation: Drop the `async` keyword if the function never awaits. Keep it only when the body uses `await`/`for await` or genuinely returns a promise.

diagnostics.title: TLS certificate verification disabled
diagnostics.recommendation: Keep verification on. If the peer uses a private CA, provide it via the `ca` option (`{ ca: fs.readFileSync('ca.pem') }`) instead of disabling verification. `rejectUnauthorized: false` accepts any certificate and enables man-in-the-middle.

diagnostics.title: Duplicate route definition
diagnostics.recommendation: Remove or merge the duplicate route — the later registration shadows the earlier one. Keep one handler per (method, path).

diagnostics.title: eval() of caller-controlled input
diagnostics.recommendation: Never eval() dynamic input. Parse structured data with JSON.parse, and replace dynamic dispatch with an explicit lookup table keyed on a validated string.

diagnostics.title: Shell command built by string interpolation
diagnostics.recommendation: Use `execFile`/`spawn` with an argument array: `execFile('git', ['clone', url])`. There is no shell to re-parse the arguments, so an interpolated value cannot become a second command.

diagnostics.title: Network call inside an open transaction
diagnostics.recommendation: Do the external I/O before the transaction (pass the result in) or after it commits — keep the `$transaction` callback pure DB work. A network round trip inside it pins the connection and holds row locks for the upstream's full latency.

diagnostics.title: Fetch-all then filter in JavaScript
diagnostics.recommendation: Move the predicate into the query's `where` (e.g. `db.user.findMany({ where: { active: true } })`) so the database returns only the rows you keep instead of streaming the whole table into JS.

diagnostics.title: Function constructor built from input
diagnostics.recommendation: Avoid the Function constructor for dynamic input — it compiles its arguments as source. Use a fixed dispatch table or a purpose-built safe expression interpreter instead.

diagnostics.title: Hardcoded credential literal
diagnostics.recommendation: Load secrets from the environment (`process.env.X`) or a secret manager (AWS Secrets Manager, Vault). Never commit a credential — it lives forever in git history and cannot be rotated without a code change.

diagnostics.title: Retry loop without backoff
diagnostics.recommendation: Add exponential backoff between attempts (`await sleep(base * 2 ** attempt)`) and a maximum-attempt cap so a downed dependency does not trigger a tight retry storm.

diagnostics.title: jwt.decode() result used for authorization
diagnostics.recommendation: Use `jwt.verify(token, key, { algorithms: [...] })` for any decision that trusts the claims. `jwt.decode` skips the signature check, so its claims are attacker-controlled.

diagnostics.title: JWT verified with the 'none' algorithm
diagnostics.recommendation: Never allow the `none` algorithm. Pin a specific allowlist, e.g. `jwt.verify(token, key, { algorithms: ['RS256'] })`, and sign with a real algorithm. `none` disables signature verification, so any token is accepted.

diagnostics.title: JSON.parse of caller input on a request path
diagnostics.recommendation: Enforce a body size limit (e.g. `express.json({ limit: '100kb' })`) before parsing, and move parsing of large payloads off the hot path (a worker thread or a streaming parser). Synchronous `JSON.parse` blocks the single event-loop thread for the whole parse.

diagnostics.title: Event listener added on every request
diagnostics.recommendation: Register listeners once at startup, or use `emitter.once(...)` inside the handler and remove it with `removeListener` when the request completes.

diagnostics.title: Math.random() used for a security token
diagnostics.recommendation: Use a CSPRNG: `crypto.randomBytes(n)` / `crypto.randomUUID()` / `crypto.randomInt()`. `Math.random()` is predictable, so any token, OTP, or session id derived from it can be guessed.

diagnostics.title: Floating database query (missing await)
diagnostics.recommendation: `await` the query (or `return` its promise, or chain `.then`/`.catch`). A bare query statement floats its promise: the write may not finish before you respond and a rejection becomes an unhandledRejection.

diagnostics.title: Body parser without a size limit
diagnostics.recommendation: Pass an explicit cap: `express.json({ limit: '1mb' })` (or the size your API actually needs). An unbounded body parser buffers the whole request in memory and is a denial-of-service / OOM vector.

diagnostics.title: Async IIFE with no error handling
diagnostics.recommendation: Attach a `.catch(err => ...)` to the invocation, or wrap the whole body in a `try/catch`. A floating async IIFE turns any rejection into an unhandledRejection, which crashes the process by default.

diagnostics.title: Stream pipe without an error handler
diagnostics.recommendation: Use `stream.pipeline(src, dest, cb)` (it forwards errors and cleans up), or attach `.on('error', handler)` to both the source and destination stream.

diagnostics.title: NoSQL operator/object injection
diagnostics.recommendation: Never pass a raw request object as a filter. Whitelist expected fields and cast each to a scalar (e.g. `String(req.body.email)`), and never build a `$where` clause from input.

diagnostics.title: Redirect to a caller-controlled URL
diagnostics.recommendation: Redirect only to a fixed allowlist of paths or origins: compare the target against a known-good set, or resolve it and assert `new URL(target).origin` is one you trust before calling redirect.

diagnostics.title: Filesystem path built from caller input without containment
diagnostics.recommendation: Resolve against a root and enforce containment: `const full = path.resolve(root, name); if (!full.startsWith(root + path.sep)) reject;` — or strip traversal with `path.basename(name)`. `join`/`resolve` normalize but do not confine.

diagnostics.title: process.exit() on a request path
diagnostics.recommendation: Never call `process.exit`/`process.abort` from a handler. Respond, then drain and shut down outside the request (`scheduleGracefulShutdown()` → `server.close()` on SIGTERM). Reserve `process.exit` for top-level fatal handlers.

diagnostics.title: Database query inside a loop (N+1)
diagnostics.recommendation: Fetch the set in one round trip: a JOIN, a `WHERE id IN (...)`, or the ORM's eager-load (`include` / `with` / `populate`). A query per iteration is N round trips for one request.

diagnostics.title: Promise.race with no timeout branch
diagnostics.recommendation: Add an explicit timeout branch to the race — a `setTimeout`/`AbortSignal.timeout(ms)` promise or a `timeout(ms)` helper — so a stuck upstream call cannot hang the race forever.

diagnostics.title: Regex with catastrophic-backtracking shape
diagnostics.recommendation: Rewrite to remove the nested quantifier (`(\w+)*` → `\w*`), anchor the pattern, or bound the tested input length. For untrusted input use a linear-time matcher (RE2) instead of the backtracking engine.

diagnostics.title: try/catch that only rethrows
diagnostics.recommendation: Remove the redundant try/catch and let the error propagate, or add real handling (log, wrap with `{ cause }`, or recover).

diagnostics.title: Response sent after calling next()
diagnostics.recommendation: Return when you delegate: `return next(err)` (or return after responding). A bare `next()` does not stop the handler, so the later `res.*` writes to an already-finished response and throws ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT.

diagnostics.title: SQL built by string interpolation
diagnostics.recommendation: Use parameter binding: `db.query('SELECT ... WHERE id = $1', [id])`, Prisma's tagged `$queryRaw` template, or the query builder. Interpolation loses the data/grammar boundary before the driver sees it.

diagnostics.title: Outbound request to a caller-controlled URL (SSRF)
diagnostics.recommendation: Validate the destination before the request: parse it with `new URL(target)` and assert its host is in an explicit allowlist, rejecting internal/link-local ranges and non-http(s) schemes.

diagnostics.title: Empty catch swallows the error
diagnostics.recommendation: Do something with the error: log it (`log.error(err)`), rethrow it (`throw err`), forward it (`next(err)`), or return a meaningful fallback. An empty catch hides the failure entirely.

diagnostics.title: Synchronous bcrypt on a request path
diagnostics.recommendation: Use the async KDF (`await bcrypt.hash(...)` / `await bcrypt.compare(...)`), which offloads the CPU-bound work to the libuv thread pool. The `*Sync` form runs the whole cost factor inline and blocks every concurrent request.

diagnostics.title: Blocking synchronous I/O on a request path
diagnostics.recommendation: Use the async form (`await fs.promises.readFile(...)`, `await execFile(...)`). The synchronous call blocks the single event-loop thread, freezing every concurrent request, the timers, and the liveness probe.

diagnostics.title: Blocking synchronous I/O reachable from a request handler
diagnostics.recommendation: Make the helper async and have the handler await it (`await fs.promises.readFile(...)`, `await execFile(...)`). A synchronous call in a helper on the request path blocks the event loop exactly as one written inline does.

diagnostics.title: throw or return inside a finally block
diagnostics.recommendation: Do not `throw` or `return` from `finally`; let the original completion of the try/catch propagate. Do side-effect cleanup (e.g. `await cleanup()`) there instead.

diagnostics.title: Secret compared with a non-constant-time operator
diagnostics.recommendation: Compare secrets in constant time: `crypto.timingSafeEqual(Buffer.from(a), Buffer.from(b))` after a length check. `===` leaks a prefix oracle through its early exit.

diagnostics.title: Express trust proxy set to unconditional true
diagnostics.recommendation: Set `trust proxy` to the exact number of proxies in front of the app (e.g. `1`), a trusted subnet string, or a predicate function — not `true`. Trusting every hop lets any client spoof `X-Forwarded-For` and thus `req.ip`.

diagnostics.title: Module-scope cache with no eviction
diagnostics.recommendation: Give the cache an eviction story: a TTL sweep (`setInterval(() => cache.clear(), ...)`), a bounded `LRUCache({ max })`, or a `WeakMap` that self-evicts. A write-only module-scope Map/Set grows without bound.

diagnostics.title: Unbounded Promise.all over a mapped collection
diagnostics.recommendation: Bound the fan-out instead of removing the parallelism: wrap each task with a concurrency limiter (`p-limit`), e.g. `collection.map((x) => limit(() => work(x)))`, so at most N run at once.

diagnostics.title: Module-scope setInterval never cleared
diagnostics.recommendation: Store the handle and `clearInterval(handle)` on shutdown, or call `handle.unref()` so the interval does not by itself keep the process alive.

diagnostics.title: RegExp constructed from caller input
diagnostics.recommendation: Never build a RegExp from raw input. Escape the value with an escape-regexp helper before interpolating it, or match against a fixed pattern and treat input as data.

diagnostics.title: vm runs untrusted code without isolation
diagnostics.recommendation: Do not treat `vm` as a sandbox. Run untrusted code in a real isolate (isolated-vm) or a separate OS process with a memory/CPU/time budget and no ambient credentials.

diagnostics.title: Weak or insecure cipher
diagnostics.recommendation: Use an authenticated cipher with a random IV: `crypto.createCipheriv('aes-256-gcm', key, iv)`. DES/3DES and RC4 are broken, ECB leaks structure, and `createCipher` derives keys insecurely.

diagnostics.title: Weak hash (MD5/SHA-1) for password storage
diagnostics.recommendation: Use a slow, salted, memory-hard KDF for passwords: `argon2.hash(pw)`, `scrypt`, or `bcrypt`. MD5/SHA-1 are GPU-crackable at billions of guesses per second.

diagnostics.title: Core module imported without the node: protocol
diagnostics.recommendation: Prefix the specifier with `node:` (e.g. `import fs from 'node:fs'`). The protocol form is unambiguous with npm packages and resolves faster.

diagnostics.title: Express app with no error-handling middleware
diagnostics.recommendation: Register a terminal error handler: `app.use((err, req, res, next) => { ... })`. Its 4-argument signature is how Express routes thrown errors and `next(err)` to your logging and shaped 500 response.

diagnostics.title: Outbound fetch without a timeout or abort signal
diagnostics.recommendation: Pass an abort signal: `fetch(url, { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(5_000) })` (Node 18+). Without it a stalled upstream pins a request slot, then a connection, then the whole pool.

diagnostics.title: jwt.verify without an algorithms allowlist
diagnostics.recommendation: Always pass an explicit allowlist, e.g. `jwt.verify(token, key, { algorithms: ['RS256'] })`. Without it, an RS256 verifier can be confused into accepting an HS256 token signed with the public key.

diagnostics.title: Unbounded findMany without a take/limit
diagnostics.recommendation: Always pass a `take` (or SQL `LIMIT`) and paginate with a cursor/offset. An unbounded `findMany` grows with the table and eventually drains the pool, the heap, and the event loop.

diagnostics.title: Cookie set without secure/httpOnly flags
diagnostics.recommendation: Set `{ httpOnly: true, secure: true, sameSite: 'lax' }` on auth cookies. `httpOnly` blocks JavaScript from reading the session (XSS theft) and `secure` keeps it off plaintext HTTP.

diagnostics.title: Server started without a SIGTERM handler
diagnostics.recommendation: On `process.on('SIGTERM', ...)`, stop accepting connections and call `server.close(() => process.exit(0))` so in-flight requests drain before the process exits.

diagnostics.title: Secret env var with a hardcoded fallback
diagnostics.recommendation: Fail fast at boot instead of degrading silently: `if (!process.env.JWT_SECRET) throw new Error('JWT_SECRET is required')`. A `|| "fallback"` ships a working key that anyone can read from source.
